_meta.description: Curated Ayurvedic Safety, Matra (Recommended Dosage), Anupana (Adjuvants), Contraindications, and Herb-Drug Interactions Reference Dataset.
_meta.sources: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API), Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, and peer-reviewed phytovigilance literature.

herbs.classical_matra: 3–6 g/day root churna (powder); 300–600 mg standardized root extract twice daily; 10–20 ml kvatha (decoction)
herbs.max_daily_matra: 6 g churna or 1200 mg standardized extract
contraindications: Pregnancy: Potential abortifacient and spasmolytic uterine effects at medicinal doses; contraindicated in gestation
Severe thyrotoxicosis / hyperthyroidism: Elevates endogenous T3 and T4 synthesis
Acute severe Pitta gastritis or peptic ulcer exacerbation due to warming (ushna virya) potency
herb_drug_interactions: Sedatives, Barbiturates, Benzodiazepines: Synergistic CNS depressant and GABAergic activity
Thyroid Hormone Therapy (Levothyroxine): Additive elevation of thyroid hormones
Immunosuppressants (Corticosteroids, Cyclosporine): Immunostimulatory properties may counteract therapy
Antidiabetic drugs: Synergistic hypoglycemic effect; monitor blood glucose levels
herbs.special_precautions: Avoid in acute liver impairment; discontinue at least 14 days before elective surgeries involving general anesthesia.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Chikitsasthana 1.1; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.classical_matra: 3–6 g/day churna; 10–20 ml fresh juice (Swarasa); 20–50 ml kvatha; 500 mg–1 g Guduchi Satva
contraindications: Autoimmune diseases in acute flare (Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Multiple Sclerosis, Rheumatoid Arthritis): Potent macrophage and immune stimulation may aggravate symptoms
Pregnancy and lactation: Limited definitive human safety data for concentrated industrial extracts
herb_drug_interactions: Immunosuppressive Agents (Cyclosporine, Tacrolimus, Azathioprine): Direct pharmacological antagonism via immune stimulation
Oral Hypoglycemics and Insulin: Enhances peripheral glucose uptake; may precipitate hypoglycemia
herbs.special_precautions: Long-term unmonitored use without lipid adjuvants (sneha) may cause mild constipation due to kashaya (astringent) rasa.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 25/40; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.botanical_name: Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica, Phyllanthus emblica
herbs.classical_matra: 3–6 g/day churna at bedtime; 1–2 tablets (500–1000 mg) twice daily; 20–40 ml decoction
herbs.max_daily_matra: 10 g/day for virechana (laxative); 3–6 g/day for routine Rasayana
anupana: Ghee and Honey in unequal proportions (for Rasayana)
contraindications: Acute diarrhea, dysentery, or acute flares of inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's, Ulcerative Colitis)
First trimester of pregnancy: Promotes downward Apana Vayu movement; theoretical mild uterine stimulation
Severe dehydration, extreme emaciation (Krisha), or acute exhaustion
herb_drug_interactions: Oral Pharmaceuticals in general: High tannin concentration binds minerals and slows intestinal drug absorption; administer 2 hours apart
Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets (Warfarin, Aspirin): Mild antiplatelet modulation by emblica tannins
herbs.special_precautions: Equal parts ghee and honey by weight is strictly contraindicated in classical Ayurveda (Viruddha Ahara); use unequal proportions.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Chikitsasthana 1.2; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.classical_matra: 1–3 g/day churna; 250–500 mg standardized extract (≥65% boswellic acids) 2–3 times daily
herbs.max_daily_matra: 3 g churna or 1500 mg standardized extract
contraindications: Pregnancy: Traditional emmenagogue and uterine stimulant properties; lack of established safety in gestation
Active erosive gastritis or severe peptic ulceration: May cause mild epigastric reflux on empty stomach
herb_drug_interactions: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Celecoxib): Dual 5-LOX and COX pathway inhibition; monitor for gastric sensitivity
Cytochrome P450 Substrates (CYP2C9, CYP3A4): Moderate in vitro enzymatic inhibition reported
herbs.special_precautions: Always ingest postprandially (after meals) to avoid gastrointestinal intolerance.
herbs.classical_source: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu Vatadi Varga; API Part I, Vol IV

herbs.classical_matra: 2–4 g/day churna; 10–20 ml fresh juice (Swarasa); 300–450 mg standardized bacosides extract daily
anupana: Cow's Ghee (Ghrita - supreme vehicle for Medhya action)
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or conduction heart block: Mild cholinergic stimulation may lower resting heart rate
Gastrointestinal tract mechanical obstruction or acute hypersecretory gastritis on empty stomach
herb_drug_interactions: Sedatives and Anxiolytics: Additive calming and psychotropic potentiating effects
Thyroid Medications: May mildly augment thyroid hormone secretion
Anticholinergic medications: Competitively counteracted by bacopa's cholinergic upregulation
herbs.special_precautions: Always take with a lipid adjuvant (ghee or whole milk) to protect gastric mucosa and facilitate blood-brain barrier transport.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 1/120; API Part I, Vol II

herbs.classical_matra: 1–3 g/day churna; 250–500 mg standardized curcumin extract 1–2 times daily; 2–5 ml fresh rhizome juice
anupana: Warm water with black pepper (Maricha for piperine)
contraindications: Biliary tract obstruction / active cholelithiasis (gallstones): Strong cholagogue action induces gallbladder contractions and may cause biliary colic
Active bleeding disorders or elective major surgery scheduled within 14 days
Severe Pitta-predominant hemorrhage (Raktapitta)
herb_drug_interactions: Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets (Warfarin, Heparin, Clopidogrel, Aspirin): Synergistic antiplatelet action increases bleeding risk
Oral Hypoglycemic Agents: Enhances insulin sensitivity; monitor for hypoglycemia
Chemotherapeutic Agents: May alter intracellular drug concentrations
herbs.special_precautions: High therapeutic doses must be avoided in acute gallbladder inflammation; co-administration with piperine increases bioavailability up to 2000%.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 27/297; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.classical_matra: 10–20 ml/day in healthy daily diet (Swasthavritta); 30–60 ml for therapeutic snehana under physician supervision
anupana: Warm water (Ushnodaka - mandatory to ensure Agni stimulation and prevent lipid indigestion)
contraindications: Ama states: Undigested endotoxins, acute fever (Nava Jwara), heavy toxic coating on tongue
Acute hepatitis, active jaundice, or acute pancreatitis
Severe Kapha aggravation with copious pulmonary mucus and productive cough
Severe uncontrolled hypertriglyceridemia (without medical supervision)
herb_drug_interactions: Lipophilic prescription drugs: Accelerates absorption and tissue bioavailability of lipophilic oral drugs
herbs.special_precautions: Never drink cold or iced water after ingesting ghee (causes severe Ajirna/indigestion and toxic Ama). Equal weights of ghee and honey is classical Viruddha Ahara (toxic combination).
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 27/231-232; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.classical_matra: 1–3 g/day leaf/bark churna; 10–20 ml decoction (kvatha); 5–10 ml fresh juice
anupana: Honey (Madhu - to mitigate intense Tikta/bitter rasa)
contraindications: Pregnancy, lactation, and couples actively planning conception: Well-documented spermicidal, anti-implantation, and abortifacient actions
Infants and small children: Oral neem seed oil can cause fatal toxic encephalopathy (Reye-like syndrome)
Severe Vata aggravation, chronic emaciation, or debility due to extreme drying (ruksha) and cooling (sheeta) properties
herb_drug_interactions: Antidiabetic medications: Potent additive blood glucose reduction; monitor blood sugar closely
Immunosuppressants: Augments cell-mediated immune responses
Lithium: May alter renal lithium clearance
herbs.special_precautions: Pure Neem seed oil (Taila) must strictly be applied externally only; never ingest pure neem oil internally.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 27/177; API Part I, Vol II

herbs.classical_matra: 3–6 g/day churna; 10–20 ml fresh juice; 300–600 mg root extract twice daily
anupana: Warm cow's milk (Dugdha - classical vehicle for Stanyajanana)
contraindications: Estrogen-receptor positive neoplasms (Breast, Ovarian, or Uterine cancer; severe Endometriosis): Phytoestrogenic saponins (shatavarins) may stimulate estrogen-sensitive tissue
Severe congestive heart failure or renal insufficiency with fluid retention (Guru/Snigdha heavy attributes)
Severe Kapha congestion and dampness
herb_drug_interactions: Diuretics (Furosemide, Spironolactone): Potential additive aquaretic/diuretic effects
Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) and Oral Contraceptives: Competitive or additive phytoestrogenic modulation
herbs.special_precautions: May cause minor bloating in patients with weak digestive fire (Mandagni) if taken without digestive spices.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Chikitsasthana 1.1; API Part I, Vol IV

herbs.classical_matra: 1–3 g/day leaf powder; 10–20 ml bark decoction; 1–2 g seed powder
contraindications: Pregnancy: Moringa root and bark contain spirochin and moringinine alkaloids that induce powerful uterine spasms and abortions; bark and root strictly contraindicated in pregnancy
Active bleeding peptic ulceration due to sharp (tikshna) and hot (ushna) qualities
Severe Pitta-Rakta disorders (burning sensation, hematuria)
herb_drug_interactions: Antihypertensive drugs: Additive blood pressure lowering
Oral Hypoglycemic Agents: Enhances glycemic control; watch for hypoglycemia
Levothyroxine: May impair gastrointestinal absorption of thyroid hormone
herbs.special_precautions: Do not consume root or root-bark preparations internally; stick strictly to leaf powder formulations.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 27/115; API Part I, Vol IV

herbs.classical_matra: 1–3 g/day purified gum resin (Shodhita Guggulu) in divided doses; 500 mg tablets 2–3 times daily
contraindications: Pregnancy and lactation: Documented emmenagogue, uterine stimulant, and potential teratogenic properties
Severe acute hepatic impairment, active acute nephritis, or inflammatory bowel disease
Active bleeding disorders, bleeding hemorrhoids, or pre-surgery
herb_drug_interactions: Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets (Warfarin, Clopidogrel, Aspirin): Potentiates antiplatelet effect and bleeding time
Lipid-Lowering Agents (Statins): Additive hypolipidemic effect; possible competition for hepatic enzymes
Oral Contraceptives: Guggulsterones induce CYP3A4 enzymes and may diminish contraceptive efficacy
herbs.special_precautions: Must strictly undergo classical Shodhana (purification in Triphala or Gomutra); raw unpurified Guggulu induces skin dermatoses, diarrhea, and liver burden.
herbs.classical_source: Sushruta Samhita Sutrasthana 45/144; API Part I, Vol I

herbs.classical_matra: 0.5–1.5 g/day churna; 250–500 mg twice daily; gradual escalation only under Vardhamana Rasayana protocol
contraindications: Chronic unpaused solitary administration: Charaka gives explicit canonical warning ('Pippali na satatam upyunjita' - continuous usage depletes Dhatus and aggravates Pitta)
Active acute gastrointestinal inflammation, peptic ulcer, hyperacidity (Amlapitta)
Active bleeding disorders (Raktapitta) due to ushna (hot) and tikshna (penetrating) potency
herb_drug_interactions: Broad Bioavailability Enhancer: Piperine strongly inhibits hepatic CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, significantly elevating blood concentrations of Phenytoin, Propranolol, Theophylline, NSAIDs, and Antibiotics
Hypoglycemics and Sedatives: Extends systemic drug circulation and potentiates therapeutic effects
herbs.special_precautions: Never take continuously beyond 2–3 weeks without a break or without an unctuous (sneha) vehicle like milk or ghee.
herbs.classical_source: Charaka Samhita Vimanasthana 1/16; API Part I, Vol IV
